name: border-shine
title: Border Shine
description: A glass edge that catches the light: a masked inset highlight whose angle follows the pointer, or the arrow keys. Wraps any card or button.
label: Border Shine (CodePen)
author: Jhey <https://codepen.io/jh3y>

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render. Use button or a for a control.

props.name: angle
props.description: Where the light sits, in degrees (0 is the top, clockwise), before the pointer moves and whenever it does not follow.

props.name: follow
props.description: Turn the light toward the pointer anywhere on the page, and with the arrow keys while the element, or a button or link inside it, has focus. Reduced motion keeps the light at angle.

props.name: squircle
props.description: Upstream's squircle corners (24% radius, a true squircle where corner-shape is supported). Turn it off to set your own radius with a rounded-* class.

props.name: className
props.description: Size, radius and fill of the plate (upstream: a 64 px square at scale 2).

a11y: Decorative edge: the highlight, the glass fill and BorderShineGlyph are aria-hidden or pseudo-elements, and the pseudo-elements ignore the pointer, so everything inside stays clickable.
Name the control: BorderShine renders a div by default; use as="button" or as="a" with an accessible name (the glyph has none).

Keyboard: while the element, or a button or link inside it, has focus, ArrowRight and ArrowUp turn the light clockwise 15 degrees (Shift: 45), ArrowLeft and ArrowDown the other way, Home resets it. Inputs, text fields and widgets that use the arrows themselves (sliders, tabs, menus, listboxes) keep their keys.
Reduced motion: the light stays at the angle prop; the pointer and the arrow keys no longer move it.
More contrast and forced colors: the highlight becomes a solid white inset line under prefers-contrast: more, and a CanvasText border under forced colors.
